description: Set high inside the Museum of Islamic Art, IDAM is Doha's most internationally decorated dining room and a rare address where museum architecture, skyline views, and Ducasse-level refinement meet. The cooking is contemporary European with regional accents, supported by a polished tasting-menu rhythm and one of the city's most memorable settings.
highlights: Michelin-starred Ducasse destination in the Museum of Islamic Art, ranked in MENA's 50 Best and overlooking Doha Bay.
restaurant_setting: Museum dining room with skyline view
sources: Michelin Guide; MENA's 50 Best Restaurants; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha

description: Jamavar brings the London-born luxury Indian restaurant language to the Sheraton Grand, with deep spice work, gracious hotel service, and a room suited to business dinners as much as celebratory nights. It is one of Doha's retained Michelin-starred restaurants and remains a reliable choice for affluent diners seeking polished Indian fine dining.
highlights: Michelin-starred Indian fine dining at the Sheraton Grand, with a formal room and refined regional dishes.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha
hotel_name_hint: Sheraton Grand Doha Resort & Convention Hotel

description: Alba is the Italian flagship at Raffles Doha and the city's newest Michelin-starred address in the 2026 guide. The restaurant combines truffle-led luxury, Riviera polish, and Katara Towers drama, making it one of the clearest special-occasion tables in modern Doha.
highlights: New 2026 Michelin one-star Italian restaurant at Raffles Doha, set inside Katara Towers in Lusail.
sources: Michelin Guide; Marhaba Qatar; Visit Qatar; The Times

description: Nobu Doha sits in a dramatic standalone building over the Arabian Gulf and remains one of the city's most recognizable luxury dining rooms. The Japanese-Peruvian menu, sea views, and Four Seasons service make it a natural alternative to a Michelin-starred reservation on a polished social night.
highlights: Landmark Gulf-facing Nobu with sushi, robata, premium seafood, and a high-energy luxury crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; The Times; Time Out Doha; Nobu Restaurants

description: Hakkasan Doha translates the brand's modern Cantonese formula into a garden-framed setting at The St. Regis Doha. It is refined enough for a formal dinner yet social enough for a long evening of dim sum, roast duck, seafood, and cocktails.
highlights: Modern Cantonese dining in a garden setting at The St. Regis, with a polished international crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Hakkasan

description: Carbone brings Major Food Group's theatrical New York Italian-American style to Al Maha Island, giving Doha a glamorous red-sauce dining room with serious social pull. It is best for diners who want luxury hospitality, familiar indulgence, and a fashionable room rather than a quiet tasting menu.
highlights: Glamorous Italian-American dining on Al Maha Island, with Carbone signatures and a dressed-up social scene.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Major Food Group

description: Zuma gives Doha a high-energy contemporary Japanese izakaya with the service, design language, and brand recognition expected by international luxury diners. The menu is built for sharing, with robata, sushi, premium seafood, and a strong evening atmosphere.
highlights: Contemporary Japanese dining on Al Maha Island, combining robata, sushi, and a fashionable late-evening mood.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; The Times; Time Out Doha

description: Morimoto Doha is a design-led Japanese destination inside Mondrian Doha, with a dramatic room, sushi bar, and the global cachet of Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto. It remains one of the strongest choices in West Bay Lagoon for affluent diners seeking polished Japanese cooking with visual impact.
highlights: Chef-branded Japanese restaurant at Mondrian Doha, known for sushi, art-filled interiors, and theatrical presentation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Mondrian Doha

description: Koo Madame is Rosewood Doha's moody, 1920s-inspired Chinese restaurant, with lacquered interiors, tableside duck, and a polished service team. It was singled out in the 2026 Michelin cycle and suits diners who want glamour, craft, and a smart Lusail setting.
highlights: Michelin-selected Chinese dining at Rosewood Doha, with Beijing duck, dark interiors, and a wine-cellar mood.
sources: Michelin Guide; Marhaba Qatar; Rosewood Doha; Taste & Flavors

description: yūn occupies the 44th floor of Waldorf Astoria Doha West Bay, giving the city a Cantonese and Taishanese restaurant with a true skyline occasion factor. The cooking is classic in spirit, while the views, tea-led drinks, and opulent room make it especially strong for date nights and visiting luxury travelers.
highlights: Skyline-view Chinese restaurant on the 44th floor of Waldorf Astoria Doha West Bay.
sources: Michelin Guide; Marhaba Qatar; Waldorf Astoria Doha West Bay

description: Shanghai Me is one of West Bay's most polished Pan-Asian rooms, blending Art Deco glamour with dim sum, sushi, wok-fired dishes, and a formal service style. Its 2026 Michelin Service Award recognition reinforces its place in the city's affluent social dining circuit.
highlights: Refined Pan-Asian restaurant in West Bay with Art Deco atmosphere, polished service, and Michelin Guide recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide; Marhaba Qatar; Shanghai Me; Time Out Doha

description: Curiosa by Jean-Georges brings a bright Latin American mood to Four Seasons Hotel Doha, with the reliability of a major international chef behind it. It is a strong choice for affluent diners who want hotel polish, spice, color, and a room that feels less formal than a tasting menu.
highlights: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's Latin restaurant at Four Seasons Hotel Doha, with polished hotel service and a lively room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; The Times; Condé Nast Traveler

description: La Mar gives Doha a beachfront Peruvian address with ceviche, anticuchos, cocktails, and a terrace-facing resort atmosphere. Gastón Acurio's name, the InterContinental setting, and the seafood-led menu make it one of the city's most credible upscale Latin American options.
highlights: Beachfront Peruvian restaurant by Gastón Acurio at InterContinental Doha, with ceviche and resort polish.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; The Times; Condé Nast Traveler

description: LPM Doha brings the Riviera-inflected Mediterranean formula to Al Maha Island, with a waterfront setting and a recognizably international clientele. It works particularly well for diners seeking a glossy, relaxed alternative to hotel fine dining.
highlights: French Mediterranean dining on Al Maha Island with water views, Riviera energy, and polished service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; LPM Restaurants

description: Gymkhana Doha adapts the London club-house Indian format to Katara Hills, with a terrace, a strong spice vocabulary, and the weight of a globally respected brand. It is a persuasive high-end Indian alternative for diners who want richness, atmosphere, and a less formal pace than a Michelin-starred table.
highlights: Luxury Indian restaurant at Katara Hills, inspired by the acclaimed London original and built for long, polished dinners.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Gymkhana
hotel_name_hint: Katara Hills Doha, LXR Hotels & Resorts

description: BiBo Doha brings Dani García's Andalusian brasserie language to the city's luxury dining scene, balancing comfort, spectacle, and Spanish technique. It is a strong option for groups who want high-end casual energy with chef-driven credibility.
highlights: Dani García Spanish brasserie with polished service, sharing dishes, and a luxury hotel audience.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha

description: Kai's Songbird brings an elegant Chinese and Nanyang-inspired menu to The Pearl, with a room that feels polished but relaxed. The restaurant has strong international pedigree through the Kai family and is a natural fit for affluent diners seeking refined Asian comfort food.
highlights: Refined Chinese and Nanyang restaurant at Corinthia Yacht Club, with polished service and a Pearl setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Kai's Songbird; Time Out Doha

description: COYA Doha delivers the brand's Peruvian sharing-menu style inside W Doha, with a glamorous room and a grown-up, high-energy crowd. It is better understood as a polished social dinner than a pure culinary temple, but the food, service, and setting clear the affluent-dining bar.
highlights: Peruvian destination at W Doha with a fashionable dining room, ceviche, grills, and strong social energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; COYA

description: Masala Library adds a theatrical, modern Indian layer to Fairmont Doha's dining mix, using familiar flavors in a more polished, design-conscious format. Its Katara Towers location gives the restaurant a strong luxury-hotel context for business and special-occasion dinners.
highlights: Modern Indian restaurant at Fairmont Doha, pairing theatrical presentation with a high-design Lusail setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Fairmont Doha

description: Rivaaj at The St. Regis Doha offers a polished Indian dining experience rooted in heritage cooking and luxury-hotel service. It is particularly useful for affluent diners who want a gracious, richly flavored meal in a quieter and more classic register than the city's louder social restaurants.
highlights: Heritage Indian restaurant at The St. Regis Doha, with polished service and a refined hotel setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Rivaaj; Time Out Doha

description: Liang is Mandarin Oriental Doha's elegant Chinese restaurant in Msheireb, with Cantonese classics and broader regional Chinese dishes in a polished downtown setting. It is a strong business-dinner and family-celebration choice for diners who want reliable luxury without theatrical excess.
highlights: Mandarin Oriental Chinese dining room in Msheireb, with Cantonese dishes and polished downtown service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Mandarin Oriental

description: MURU adds a polished Nikkei and live-fire perspective to Waldorf Astoria Doha West Bay, with premium cuts, seafood, and a glossy hotel context. The restaurant suits diners who want the structure of a serious dinner with a more social, modern atmosphere.
highlights: Michelin-selected Nikkei and grill restaurant at Waldorf Astoria Doha West Bay, with premium cuts and a polished room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Waldorf Astoria Doha West Bay

description: SAWA by Sanad is a refined Levantine restaurant inside one of Msheireb's most polished hospitality addresses. The room has private-club discretion, while the cooking offers a more elevated and design-conscious expression of Middle Eastern dining.
highlights: Modern Levantine restaurant in Msheireb with private-club atmosphere and refined regional cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Sanad; Time Out Doha

description: TONO by Akira Back brings Nikkei energy to Porto Arabia, with a waterfront terrace and a menu that leans into Japanese technique, Latin brightness, and sharing formats. It is one of The Pearl's strongest high-end casual dinner choices for visitors and residents alike.
highlights: Nikkei restaurant by Akira Back at Porto Arabia, with waterfront terrace seating and a polished sharing menu.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha

description: Chicago Rare is a premium steakhouse at Four Seasons The Pearl, styled with vintage American glamour and a serious grill program. It fills an important affluent-dining niche in Doha for diners seeking beef, seafood, classic service, and a waterfront resort setting.
highlights: Luxury steakhouse at Four Seasons The Pearl, with vintage Chicago styling, premium beef, seafood, and terrace views.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha; Chicago Rare
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Resort and Residences at The Pearl-Qatar

description: Jiwan is one of Doha's most meaningful modern Qatari restaurants, set on the fourth floor of the National Museum of Qatar with sweeping views across the Corniche and port. The cooking reimagines local flavors in a refined but relaxed way, making it essential for visitors who want a true sense of place.
highlights: Modern Qatari restaurant at the National Museum of Qatar, with terrace views and a Ducasse-linked sense of refinement.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Condé Nast Traveler; The Times

description: Berenjak Al Maha Island turns Persian kababs, breads, stews, and tea culture into a polished island dining experience with views across the Gulf and Doha skyline. Its Bib Gourmand recognition does not make it formal fine dining, but the setting and execution make it a strong relaxed-night choice for affluent diners.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand Persian restaurant on Al Maha Island, with charcoal-grilled kababs and Gulf views.
sources: Michelin Guide; Berenjak; Discover Qatar; Visit Qatar

description: The Salt Road at Andaz Doha gives West Bay a more distinctive chef-driven alternative to standard hotel international dining. The menu builds around South African technique, salt, curing, pickling, Josper fire, and Cape-influenced flavors, making it a useful choice for curious luxury diners.
highlights: South African-inspired restaurant at Andaz Doha, focused on salt, preservation, fire cooking, and polished hotel dining.
sources: Michelin Guide; Visit Qatar; Hyatt; En Primeur Club

description: Babel Qatar brings polished Lebanese seafood and mezze to St. Regis Marsa Arabia Island, with the glossy service and waterfront context expected from the address. It is a strong high-end Middle Eastern choice for diners who want generous flavors in a luxury resort environment.
highlights: Luxury Lebanese restaurant at St. Regis Marsa Arabia Island, with seafood, mezze, and a polished waterfront setting.
sources: Time Out Doha; Visit Qatar; Babel Qatar; St. Regis Marsa Arabia Island
hotel_name_hint: The St. Regis Marsa Arabia Island, The Pearl-Qatar

description: Em Sherif Restaurant gives Al Maha Island a luxurious Lebanese dining room built for family-style feasts, terrace views, and a dressed-up Middle Eastern crowd. The cooking is traditional in spirit, but the service, interiors, and setting place it firmly in Doha's affluent social-dining conversation.
highlights: Elegant Lebanese restaurant on Al Maha Island, with a covered terrace, skyline views, and generous sharing dishes.
sources: Michelin Guide; Em Sherif Restaurant; Visit Qatar; Time Out Doha

description: Bayt Sharq is a restored Qatari heritage house near the Corniche, complete with traditional rooms, a small museum, and a courtyard sense of old Doha. It is informal compared with the hotel dining rooms, but it gives sophisticated visitors a culturally meaningful dinner rooted in Qatari cooking.
highlights: Traditional Qatari restaurant in a restored century-old Al Khulaifi house near the Corniche.
sources: Michelin Guide; Time Out Doha; The Times; Condé Nast Traveler

description: SMAT is a refined Qatari and Gulf restaurant at the southern end of the Corniche, combining generous local dishes with a more polished, opulent room than a casual heritage kitchen. It works well for diners who want regional flavors, a waterfront-adjacent setting, and enough comfort for an adult evening meal.
highlights: Polished Qatari and Gulf restaurant at Oriental Pearl on the Corniche, with generous dishes and refined local flavor.
sources: Michelin Guide; SMAT; Time Out Doha; Visit Qatar

description: Saasna, meaning our roots in Qatari dialect, preserves local recipes in a contemporary Msheireb setting. It is relaxed rather than luxurious, but its cultural role, proper dinner format, and modern presentation make it one of Doha's most important local-favorite inclusions.
highlights: Contemporary Qatari restaurant in Msheireb, dedicated to preserving local culinary heritage with modern flair.
sources: Michelin Guide; Al Sraiya Hospitality; Condé Nast Traveler; Time Out Doha

description: Parisa Souq Waqif is one of Doha's most atmospheric classic dining rooms, famous for its mirrored Persian interior, mosaic work, and charcoal-grilled dishes. It remains a valuable relaxed-night choice for affluent visitors who want a richly local setting without defaulting to a hotel restaurant.
highlights: Ornate Persian restaurant in Souq Waqif, known for mirrored interiors, grilled meats, and old-market atmosphere.
sources: Condé Nast Traveler; The Times; Time Out Doha; Parisa Restaurants

description: Ard Canaan is a beloved Palestinian and Levantine restaurant in Katara Cultural Village, with a palace-like interior and a strong following among local diners. It is not a fine-dining restaurant, but the setting, hospitality, and regional cooking make it an excellent relaxed dinner for a well-traveled visitor.
highlights: Popular Palestinian and Levantine restaurant in Katara Cultural Village, with grand interiors and a local following.
sources: Time Out Doha; Ard Canaan; Qatar Arab Local; Restaurant Guru
